newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon minister denies wiretapping charges.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon minister denies wiretapping charges.

text.p: Lebanon's Interior Minister Michel al-Murr denied on Wednesday allegations that security or military organs were involved in tapping cellular telephone calls.
"Military and security organs are not tapping the cellular (network) in any way," Murr told reporters in parliament.
"As for the private operating companies, we cannot say whether they are tapping or not," he added.

Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri last week ordered an investigation into charges by former prime minister Selim al-Hoss, who is now an opposition member of parliament, that equipment for intercepting cellular telephone calls had recently been installed in Lebanon.
The government has not yet formally replied to Hoss's charges which were made in a parliamentary question.
Hariri has asked Defence Minister Mohsen Dalloul to inform him of measures he would take if investigations proved that security organs were involved in illegal wiretapping.
Wiretapping is only permitted in Lebanon on authorisation of a judge.
Officials of Libancell and Cellis, the two cellular telephone companies set up by Finland Telecom and France Telecom in Lebanon, have said they were not aware of any wiretapping.

The two cellular networks have grown rapidly since their introduction in 1994. They now have some 200,000 subscribers and rival the normal telephone network which is still being repaired after the 1975-90 civil war.
